bullets.content: Check the root tag and format first: the file must open with <root BTCPP_format="4"> and hold at least one <BehaviorTree ID="..."> block, with MainTree as the entry tree by convention.
A decorator owns exactly one child: Inverter, ForceSuccess, ForceFailure, Repeat, Retry and Timeout with zero or two children fail the checker, so nest one child only.
A SubTree tag must carry an ID that names a BehaviorTree block in the same file and must not have children; an unknown or empty ID is the common XML refusal.

Sequence stops at the first FAILURE or RUNNING and Fallback stops at the first SUCCESS or RUNNING; ReactiveSequence and ReactiveFallback restart at the first child each tick so an earlier child can preempt a RUNNING later child.
CONDITION answers SUCCESS or FAILURE only, never RUNNING, and must not change the world; ACTION may answer RUNNING and must implement halt(), while SyncActionNode never answers RUNNING.

halt() returns a RUNNING node to IDLE: control nodes halt RUNNING children with haltChildren(), decorators halt the single child with haltChild(), and a finished ACTION keeps SUCCESS or FAILURE until reset.

Run python scripts/behavetree_how.py --input <tree.xml> --out <file>: stdout starts OK with exit 0 and writes tree ids plus node count, or starts ERROR with exit 2 and writes nothing on missing file, bad XML, or refused path.
